With scope: 'worker' each attempt gets a new browser context, and a Kernel profile applies only to the browser's default context, so it has no effect. With scope: 'attempt' each attempt leases a new browser and runs in its default context, so the profile applies.
The step is blocked with AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED.

Return a blocked verdict with STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, STEP_TIMEOUT or CANCELLED only when the budget is spent, the deadline passed or the test was cancelled. The runner refuses any other use, and a passed verdict with a code, with MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID.

Exit code 3: a test failure is 1 and an infrastructure failure is 3, and in a mixed run the highest-precedence code wins (130 > 4 > 3 > 2 > 1 > 0). The report keeps every individual result; precedence affects only the process exit code.

Bitrise: add the key under Secrets in the app's workflow editor; a pull request build gets it only when Expose for Pull Requests is on, and a public app's build never does. EAS Workflows: keep it in an EAS environment variable with secret visibility and set environment: on each job (a custom job reads production by default); every job that reads that environment can read the key, including one running an untrusted pull request.

For each remaining finding it writes a repro test that asserts the expected behavior and runs it; the finding is a bug only when the test fails with ASSERTION_FAILED. Repro tests are tagged bugbash, so run the gating run with --exclude-tag bugbash; after the fix, remove the tag and keep the test as a regression test.
